headline: President Obama created an emergency board to look into labor disputes between New Jersey Transit Rail and some of its unionized workers.
what_it_does: This order sets up an emergency board to investigate disputes between New Jersey Transit Rail and certain employees represented by labor unions. Emergency boards like this are used under federal railway labor law to study a dispute and suggest how to settle it. While a board is working, the law generally keeps both sides from striking or locking out workers for a set period. The title alone does not give details on the specific issues in the dispute.

who_it_affects.group: New Jersey Transit Rail employees represented by the unions in the dispute
who_it_affects.how: Their dispute with the railroad is reviewed by a federal board, and a strike is generally put on hold while that happens.
The agency must take part in the board's investigation and generally cannot change working conditions or lock out workers during the review period.
Commuter rail service is likely to keep running without a strike while the board does its work.
